{{Short description|Type of directed hypergraph}}

[[File:BF-graph.svg|thumb|Each blue hyperedge has all tails but one, making them '''B-arcs'''. Likewise, each orange edge has all heads but one, making them '''F-arcs'''. A '''BF-graph''' consists only of these two kinds of directed arcs, such as the one shown.]]

In [[graph theory]], a '''BF-graph''' is a type of [[directed graph|directed]] [[hypergraph]] where each [[hyperedge]] is directed either to one particular [[vertex (graph theory)|vertex]] or away from one particular vertex.<ref name="Gallo1993">{{Cite journal
| author = G. Gallo
| author2 = G. Longo
| author3 = S. Nguyen
| author4 = S. Pallottino
| name-list-style = amp
| title = Directed hypergraphs and applications
| journal = Discrete Applied Mathematics
| url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/81159246.pdf
| doi = 10.1016/0166-218X(93)90045-P
| volume = 42
| number = 2–3
| year = 1993
| pages = 177–201
}}</ref>

== Definition ==
In a directed hypergraph, each hyperedge may be directed away from some of its vertices (its ''tails'') and towards some others of its vertices (its ''heads'').
A hyperedge that is directed to a single head vertex, and away from all its other vertices, is called a ''B''-arc (backward arc). Symmetrically, a hyperedge that is directed away from a single tail vertex, and towards all its other vertices, is called an ''F''-arc (forward arc).<ref name="Gallo1993"/>

A hypergraph with only B-arcs is a '''B-graph''' (or B-hypergraph) and a hypergraph with only F-arcs is a '''F-graph''' (or F-hypergraph). A '''BF-graph''' (or BF-hypergraph) is a hypergraph whose hyperarcs are either B-arcs or F-arcs.<ref name="Gallo1993"/><ref name="Nguyen1998">{{Cite journal
 |author1=S. Nguyen
 |author2=D. Pretolani
 |author3=L. Markenzon
 |name-list-style=amp
 |title = On Some Path Problems on Oriented Hypergraphs
 |journal = Informatique Théorique et Applications
 |volume = 32
 |number = 1–3
 |year = 1998
 |pages = 1–20
 |url = http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ITA_1998__32_1-3_1_0
}}</ref><ref name="Guedes2005">{{Cite journal
 |author1=A.L.P. Guedes
 |author2=L. Markenzon
 |name-list-style=amp
 |title = Directed Hypergraph Planarity
 |journal = Pesquisa Operacional
 |volume = 25

 |year = 2005
 |pages = 383–390
 |doi = 10.1590/S0101-74382005000300005

|doi-access = free

== Properties ==
Any general directed hypergraph can be transformed into a BF-graph by adding a dummy node to each hyperarc that is neither a B-arc nor an F-arc, thus replacing each such hyperarc with one B-arc and one F-arc.<ref name="Gallo1993"/>

The symmetric image of a B-graph is an F-graph, and vice versa. This is obtained by reversing the direction of all hyperarcs.<ref name="Gallo1993"/>

== Paths and connectivity ==
In BF-graphs, different types of paths and connectivity can be defined:

* A '''B-path''' (or B-hyperpath) from node ''s'' to node ''t'' is a minimal hypergraph where every node is connected to ''s'' by means of a cycle-free simple path
* An '''F-path''' (or F-hyperpath) from ''s'' to ''t'' is a hypergraph whose symmetric image is a B-path from ''t'' to ''s''
* A '''BF-path''' (or BF-hyperpath) from ''s'' to ''t'' is a hypergraph that is simultaneously both a B-path and an F-path from ''s'' to ''t''

Correspondingly, nodes can be B-connected, F-connected, or BF-connected depending on whether the respective type of path exists between them.<ref name="Gallo1993"/><ref name="Nguyen1998"/>

== Applications ==
Directed hypergraphs and their BF-graph subfamily have found applications across diverse areas of [[computer science]], including database systems, expert systems, parallel programming, scheduling, routing in dynamic networks, [[data mining]], and [[bioinformatics]].<ref name="Guedes2005"/>

=== B-graphs ===
B-graphs have been particularly useful in representing [[Horn clause|Horn formulae]] in [[propositional logic]], where they are sometimes called "labelled graphs". They have also been applied to analyzing [[deductive database]]s and studying Leontiev substitution matrices and flow problems.<ref name="Gallo1993"/>

=== F-graphs ===
F-graphs have found applications in urban transit problems, particularly for modeling passenger distribution in transit systems. They have also been used in the analysis of [[And-or tree|And-Or graphs]] in [[artificial intelligence]].<ref name="Gallo1993"/>

=== BF-graphs ===
BF-graphs provide a general framework that can model concurrent systems and parallel computation programs. They are particularly useful for representing task precedence and simultaneous execution in synchronous systems.<ref name="Nguyen1998"/> The structure has also been applied to scheduling problems and routing in dynamic networks.<ref name="Guedes2005"/>

BF-graphs are well-suited for representing [[functional dependency|functional dependencies]] in [[relational database]]s, as both the domain and codomain of a functional dependency may contain multiple attributes. This property has been utilized in converting relational databases to [[Resource Description Framework]] (RDF) representations for [[semantic web]] applications.<ref name="Ghaleb2020">{{Cite journal
 |author1=F.F.M. Ghaleb
 |author2=A.A. Taha
 |author3=M. Hazman
 |author4=M. Abd ElLatif
 |author5=M. Abbass
 |name-list-style=amp
 |title = RDF-BF-Hypergraph Representation for Relational Database
 |journal = International Journal of Mathematics and Computer Science
 |volume = 15
 |number = 1
 |year = 2020
 |pages = 41–64
 |url = https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352440890_RDF-BF-Hypergraph_Representation_for_Relational_Database
}}</ref>

== Computational complexity ==
Several path problems that are polynomial-time solvable on ordinary directed graphs become [[NP-hard]] when extended to BF-graphs. For example, finding a minimum cardinality B-path in a B-graph is NP-hard, even though the corresponding shortest path problem in ordinary graphs can be solved in polynomial time.<ref name="Gallo1993"/> However, certain special cases and constrained versions of these problems remain tractable.<ref name="Nguyen1998"/>

In contrast, planarity testing for BF-graphs can be performed efficiently in linear time with respect to the size of the hypergraph.<ref name="Guedes2005"/>
